title: Proportional Rollout Throttler & Reliability Priority Economizer
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a Console-level orchestration feature that throttles and phases initiative rollouts across services based on a proportional economic model of remaining error budget, customer impact weighting, and expected cost of remediation. The goal is to avoid single-initiative blasts that exhaust shared error budgets while automatically prioritizing and pacing canary traffic for initiatives with higher customer impact and lower unit-cost trade-offs. This will tie into the error-budget ledger, per-route SLI telemetry, and the rollout APIs for canary sizing and auto-fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI shows a ranked list of active initiatives with computed 'throttle score' derived from remaining error budget, customer impact, and cost-to-fix estimate
Can configure per-initiative target throttles (0-100%) and a global proportional policy that enforces budget-aware pacing
Rollout controller respects proportional throttle decisions and exposes audit events for each traffic allocation change
Integration test simulating concurrent initiatives demonstrates preserved SLOs in 3/3 Monte Carlo runs under typical load profiles
Telemetry: time-series of error budget burn rate, per-initiative throttle percentage, and linked cost delta visible in Console
tasks: Design policy model: formula for throttle_score = f(remaining_error_budget, customer_impact, cost_to_fix, recent_sli_trend)
Prototype simulation harness (Monte Carlo) to validate pacing under realistic traffic mixes
Console UI: initiative leaderboard, manual override, and policy toggle
API: endpoint to return recommended throttle percentages and to accept operator overrides
Rollout integrations: add hooks to canary controller to receive throttle updates and emit audit logs
QA: inject synthetic SLI regressions and validate automated pacing prevents budget exhaustion
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created after reliability guild workshop. Problem statement: multiple teams pushing canaries concurrently caused a cross-service error-budget spike last quarter.
2026-03-11 Alejandro Ruiz: Scoped the policy inputs. Suggested starting weights: remaining_error_budget(0.5), customer_impact(0.3), cost_to_fix(0.2). Will iterate after prototype.

2026-03-12 Priya Patel (SRE): Raised concern about data latency for SLI signals; recommended 30s aggregated windows to avoid oscillation. Also requested explicit cooldown windows for throttle changes.
2026-03-13 Design review: Liam O'Connor suggested a compact leaderboard card in Console and a 'panic' button to pause all non-critical initiatives. Design will hand off mockups by 2026-03-18.

2026-03-14 Engineering note: Blocker - rollout controller does not yet surface per-initiative audit hooks. ENG-20021 (internal) created to add audit webhook. Punting API contract until hook is available.

2026-03-15 Alejandro Ruiz: Ran small Monte Carlo prototype. Early results show proportional policy reduces peak simultaneous burns by ~38% vs naive FIFO rollout. Need to tune cost_to_fix estimates; product to propose a method for deriving those from recent incident tickets and estimated engineer-hours.
decisions: Use a continuous throttle percentage (0-100) rather than binary allow/deny to enable smooth pacing
Initial throttle formula will weight SLI trend smoothing with a 3-window exponential moving average to prevent flip-flopping
Customer impact will be a manually-curated score (0-5) per initiative for Q1, migrate to automated signal in Q2
Default policy will auto-fallback to 'conservative' mode when global error budget hits 20% remaining
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive throttling favors SLO stability but increases time-to-value for product experiments. We'll expose an escalation path for product owners to request temporary exceptions with justification.
Potential future: surface suggested cost_to_fix using ticket history and oncall estimates; add machine-learned forecast for SLI delta per percent of traffic.
Fallback policy should be pluggable so Dedicated/Private customers can substitute corporate-wide rules.
